title: A circular queue in an array
summary: front and rear chase each other around the array. The % operator wraps them back to cell 0.

checkpoints.text: The queue is full: 1, 2, 3, 4, with `front` at cell 0 and `rear` at cell 3.
Dequeue takes the value at `front` (1) and moves `front` one cell right. Cell 0 is free now, but it is behind `front`.
Enqueuing 5: `rear` is at cell 3, the last one. (3 + 1) % 4 is 0, so `rear` wraps around to cell 0, the free space at the start.
5 is stored in cell 0. In array order the cells read 5, 2, 3, 4, but the 2 in cell 1 was already dequeued. In queue order it is 3, 4, 5: from `front` around to `rear`.
6 went into cell 1. Without wrapping around, the freed cells at the start could never be used again, and the queue would "fill up" after only four enqueues in total.
